ID: sec:doc:federal_regulation:42-CFR-438:438.8
Title: Medical loss ratio (MLR) standards
Section: 438.8
Policy: 42-CFR-438
Type: federal_regulation
Last revised: 2024-05-10
Federal Register cite: [81 FR 27853, May 6, 2016, as amended at 82 FR 39, Jan. 3, 2017; 85 FR 72840, Nov. 13, 2020; 89 FR 41272, May 10, 2024]
Citation link: [42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)
Reason: Primary MLR calculation or reporting section from the governing regulation.
Content:
(a) Basic rule. The State must ensure, through its contracts starting on or after July 1, 2017, that each MCO, PIHP, and PAHP calculate and report a MLR in accordance with this section. For multi-year contracts that do not start in 2017, the State must require the MCO, PIHP, or PAHP to calculate and report a MLR for the rating period that begins in 2017.

(b) Definitions. As used in this section, the following terms have the indicated meanings:

Credibility adjustment means an adjustment to the MLR for a partially credible MCO, PIHP, or PAHP to account for a difference between the actual and target MLRs that may be due to random statistical variation.

Full credibility means a standard for which the experience of an MCO, PIHP, or PAHP is determined to be sufficient for the calculation of a MLR with a minimal chance that the difference between the actual and target medical loss ratio is not statistically significant. An MCO, PIHP, or PAHP that is assigned full credibility (or is fully credible) will not receive a credibility adjustment to its MLR.

Member months mean the number of months an enrollee or a group of enrollees is covered by an MCO, PIHP, or PAHP over a specified time period, such as a year.

MLR reporting year means a period of 12 months consistent with the rating period selected by the State.

No credibility means a standard for which the experience of an MCO, PIHP, or PAHP is determined to be insufficient for the calculation of a MLR. An MCO, PIHP, or PAHP that is assigned no credibility (or is non-credible) will not be measured against any MLR requirements.

Non-claims costs means those expenses for administrative services that are not: Incurred claims (as defined in paragraph (e)(2) of this section); expenditures on activities that improve health care quality (as defined in paragraph (e)(3) of this section); or licensing and regulatory fees, or Federal and State taxes (as defined in paragraph (f)(2) of this section).

Partial credibility means a standard for which the experience of an MCO, PIHP, or PAHP is determined to be sufficient for the calculation of a MLR but with a non-negligible chance that the difference between the actual and target medical loss ratios is statistically significant. An MCO, PIHP, or PAHP that is assigned partial credibility (or is partially credible) will receive a credibility adjustment to its MLR.

(c) MLR requirement. If a State elects to mandate a minimum MLR for its MCOs, PIHPs, or PAHPs, that minimum MLR must be equal to or higher than 85 percent (the standard used for projecting actuarial soundness under § 438.4(b)) and the MLR must be calculated and reported for each MLR reporting year by the MCO, PIHP, or PAHP, consistent with this section.

(d) Calculation of the MLR. The MLR experienced for each MCO, PIHP, or PAHP in a MLR reporting year is the ratio of the numerator (as defined in paragraph (e) of this section) to the denominator (as defined in paragraph (f) of this section). A MLR may be increased by a credibility adjustment, in accordance with paragraph (h) of this section.

(e) Numerator —(1) Required elements. The numerator of an MCO's, PIHP's, or PAHP's MLR for a MLR reporting year is the sum of the MCO's, PIHP's, or PAHP's incurred claims (as defined in (e)(2) of this section); the MCO's, PIHP's, or PAHP's expenditures for activities that improve health care quality (as defined in paragraph (e)(3) of this section); and fraud prevention activities (as defined in paragraph (e)(4) of this section).

(2) Incurred claims. (i) Incurred claims must include the following:

(A) Direct claims that the MCO, PIHP, or PAHP paid to providers (including under capitated contracts with network providers) for services or supplies covered under the contract and services meeting the requirements of § 438.3(e) provided to enrollees.

(B) Unpaid claims liabilities for the MLR reporting year, including claims reported that are in the process of being adjusted or claims incurred but not reported.

(C) Withholds from payments made to network providers.

(D) Claims that are recoverable for anticipated coordination of benefits.

(E) Claims payments recoveries received as a result of subrogation.

(F) Incurred but not reported claims based on past experience, and modified to reflect current conditions, such as changes in exposure or claim frequency or severity.

(G) Changes in other claims-related reserves.

(H) Reserves for contingent benefits and the medical claim portion of lawsuits.

(ii) Amounts that must be deducted from incurred claims include the following:

(A) Overpayment recoveries received from network providers.

(B) Prescription drug rebates received and accrued.

(iii) Expenditures that must be included in incurred claims include the following:

(A) The amount of incentive and bonus payments made, or expected to be made, to network providers that are tied to clearly-defined, objectively measurable, and well-documented clinical or quality improvement standards that apply to providers.

(B) The amount of claims payments recovered through fraud reduction efforts, not to exceed the amount of fraud reduction expenses. The amount of fraud reduction expenses must not include activities specified in paragraph (e)(4) of this section.

(C) The amount of payments made to providers under State directed payments described in § 438.6(c).

(iv) Amounts that must either be included in or deducted from incurred claims include, respectively, net payments or receipts related to State mandated solvency funds.

(v) Amounts that must be excluded from incurred claims:

(A) Non-claims costs, as defined in paragraph (b) of this section, which include the following:

( 1 ) Amounts paid to third party vendors for secondary network savings.

( 2 ) Amounts paid to third party vendors for network development, administrative fees, claims processing, and utilization management.

Title: ddddd. Section V. B. Medicaid, 7. Financial Requirements, ii. Medical Loss Ratio is revised and restated in its entirety as follows:
Type: managed_care_contract
Citation link: [Contract #30-2020-052-DHB-TP Amendment 5/7](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/contract-30-2020-052-dhb-tp-amendment-57/download?attachment)
Reason: State implementation section from the NC policy document named by the question.
Content:
Medical Loss Ratio
(i) The Medical Loss Ratio (MLR) standards are to ensure the BH I/DD Tailored Plan is directing a sufficient portion of the capitation payments received from the Department to services and activities that improve health in alignment with the Department's program goals and objectives.
(ii) The BH I/DD Tailored Plan shall calculate and report aggregate MLR on an annual basis aligned to the rating year on two (2) bases as follows:
(a) The BH I/DD Tailored Plan shall calculate the CMS-defined MLR experienced in a MLR reporting year as defined in 42 C.F.R. § 438.8 and 42 C.F.R § 457.1203(c)-(f).
The CMS-defined MLR shall be reported in aggregate combined for Medicaid Expansion Eligible Member and non-Medicaid Expansion populations.
The numerator of the BH I/DD Tailored Plan's CMS -defined MLR for a MLR reporting year shall be defined as the sum of the BH I/DD Tailored Plan's incurred claims, expenditures for activities that improve health care quality, and the lesser of expenditures for fraud reduction activities or fraud reduction recoveries as defined in 42 C.F.R. § 438.8(e).
The denominator of the BH I/DD Tailored Plan's CMS -defined MLR for a MLR reporting year shall equal the BH I/DD Tailored Plan's adjusted premium revenue. The adjusted premium revenue shall be defined as the BH I/DD Tailored Plan's premium revenue minus the BH I/DD Tailored Plan's federal, state, and local taxes and licensing and regulatory fees as defined in 42 C.F.R. § 438.8(f).
(b) The  BH  I/DD  Tailored  Plan  shall  calculate  the  Department-defined  MLR  experienced  for  all  Non-Expansion populations in a MLR reporting year as the ratio of the numerator and denominator.
Reserved.
The numerator of the Department-defined MLR shall be calculated in a manner similar to the CMS-defined MLR with the following adjustments:
The BH I/DD Tailored Plan is permitted to include expenditures made for voluntary contributions to health-related resources and initiatives that advance public health and Health Equity that align with the Department's Quality Strategy and meet the followin g conditions:
Meet standards established in the Department's Quality Strategy that such contributions reflect meaningful  engagement  with  local  communities  and  are  non-discriminatory  with  respect  to individual members and North Carolina geographic areas, including rural areas.
Meet standards established in the Department's Quality Strategy that the expenditures are spent directly  on  improving  outcomes  for  beneficiaries,  such  as  housing  initiatives  or  support  for community-based organizations that provide meals, transportation or other essential services.
The BH I/DD Tailored Plan is prohibited from including in the Department-defined MLR numerator any of the following expenditures:
Required additional directed payments to providers as required in the Contract and allowed under 42 C.F.R. § 438.6(c)(1)(iii)(B)  or  other  wrap payments, that are reimbursed by the Department separate from the prospective PMPM capitation and maternity event payments.
Payments to related providers that violate the Payment Limitations as required in the Contract.
The denominator of the Department-defined MLR shall be calculated in a manner similar to the CMSdefined MLR with the following adjustment:
Payments from the Department to reimburse for required additional directed or wrap payments to providers shall be subtracted from the denominator along with any associated taxes and fees.
(iii) The following requirements apply to both the CMS-defined MLR and the Department-defined MLR:
(a) The  BH  I/DD  Tailored  Plan's  classification  of  activities  that  improve  health  care  quality,  and  initiatives  that advance public health and Health Equity, shall be subject to Department review and approval.
(b) The BH I/DD Tailored Plan shall ensure that the following expenditures are excluded from the numerator in both the CMS-defined MLR and Department-defined MLR:
Interest or penalty payments to providers for failure to meet prompt payment standards;
Fines and penalties assessed by the Department or other regulatory authorities;
Rebates paid to the Department if the BH I/DD Tailored Plan's Department -defined MLR is less than the minimum MLR threshold for a prior year;
Voluntary contributions to health-related resources or initiatives that advance Health Equity made in lieu of rebates paid to the Department if the BH I/DD Tailored Plan's Department -defined MLR is less than the minimum MLR threshold for  a  prior  year  as  described  in Sections  V.B.7.ii.(iv) and V.B.7.ii.(ix)(c) of  this Contract;
The BH I/DD Tailored Plan shall exclude from the MLR numerator any non-claims costs defined in 42 C.F.R. §  438.8(e)(2)(v)(A),  PBM  fees  and  spread  pricing,  marketing  or  branding  material,  related  party administrative  payments  and  margin,  and  administrative  costs  not  allowed  as  health  care  quality improvement including corporate allocations; and
Voluntary contributions to health-related resources or initiatives that advance Health Equity made in lieu of remittances paid to the Department if the PIHP's risk corridor measurement resulted in a payment to the Department for a prior year, as described in Sections V.B.7.v.(i)(j)ix. and V.B.7.v.(ii)(c)x .
(c) The BH I/DD Tailored Plan shall aggregate data for all Medicaid eligibility groups covered under the Contract for purposes  of  calculating  the  CMS-defined  MLR  and  all  Non-Expansion  eligibility  groups  for  the  Departmentdefined MLR.
(d) The BH I/DD Tailored Plan shall use a credibility adjustment, as defined in 42 C.F.R. § 438.8(h)(1)-(3), for plans with less than 380,000 member months in a MLR reporting year.
(e) Payments  related  to  the  Healthy  Opportunities  Pilot  Program  shall  not  be  incorporated  into  the  capitation payment nor into the MLR, unless otherwise required by CMS.

Title: i. Disenrollment from BH I/DD Tailored Plans and Medicaid Managed Care
Type: managed_care_contract
Citation link: [Contract #30-2020-052-DHB-TP Amendment 5/7](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/contract-30-2020-052-dhb-tp-amendment-57/download?attachment)
Reason: State implementation section from the NC policy document named by the question.
Content:
Member disenrollment from the BH I/DD Tailored Plan may occur pursuant to specific criteria described in this Policy, which may include complete disenrollment from Medicaid Managed Care or disenrolling from a BH I/DD Tailored Plan to a Standard Plan.
Member requested disenrollment
A member, or an authorized representative, may submit a verbal or written request for disenrollment from the BH I/DD Tailored Plan to the Enrollment Broker by phone, mail, inperson, or electronically.
A member who is not excluded from Standard Plan enrollment may request disenrollment from a BH I/DD Tailored Plan and transfer to a Standard Plan or the EBCI Tribal Option (if applicable) any time during the coverage year. 11 2
A member who is excluded from Standard Plan enrollment may request disenrollment from a BH I/DD Tailored Plan and transfer  to  NC Medicaid Direct  any  time during  the coverage year.
10 2 There may be instances (e.g., an urgent medical need), as determined by the Department and based on the beneficiary's needs, in which enrollment in the new PHP or the new delivery system may become effective sooner, including mid-month.
11 1 Members enrolled in the Innovations or TBI waivers must disenroll from their respective waiver before they can disenroll from a BH I/DD Tailored Plan.
The member, or the authorized representative, must contact the Enrollment Broker in order to initiate a disenrollment request.
At the time of the disenrollment request, choice counseling for the member or his or her representative will be available from the Enrollment Broker.
The  Enrollment  Broker  will  process  disenrollment  requests  in  accordance  with  the following:
The Enrollment Broker will evaluate the request and will approve it if the member is not enrolled in the Innovations or TBI waiver.
The Enrollment Broker will notify the Department of its decision by the next business day following receipt of the request.
Notice of disenrollment determination
The Department will notify the member or authorized representative, and the BH I/DD Tailored Plan of the approval or denial of the disenrollment request and, if approved, the disenrollment will be effective the first day of the month following receipt of the request by the Enrollment Broker.
The effective date of an approved disenrollment request will be no later than the first day of the second month following the month in which the member requests disenrollment. If the  Enrollment  Broker  or the Department fails to make a disenrollment determination within the specified timeframes, the disenrollment is considered approved for the first day of the following month unless there is an urgent need. 12 1
Expedited review of member initiated requests for disenrollment
A member, or an authorized representative, may request an expedited review of his or her disenrollment request when the member has an urgent medical need. For purposes of this subsection, an urgent medical need means continued enrollment in the BH I/DD Tailored Plan could jeopardize the member's life, physical or mental health, or ability to attain, maintain, or regain maximum function.
The Enrollment Broker will process requests for expedited review in accordance with the following:
The Enrollment Broker will transmit expedited review requests to the Department for evaluation within twelve (12) hours of receipt of the request.
The  Department  will  evaluate  and  decide  whether  to  approve  or  deny  the request.
The Department will notify the member, or authorized representative, and the BH I/DD Tailored Plan of the approval or denial of the expedited disenrollment request. If approved, the disenrollment effective date, will be within three (3) calendar days of receipt of the request by the Enrollment Broker.
Disenrollment required by the Department
The Department may disenroll a member from Medicaid Managed Care for any of the following reasons:
(a) Loss of eligibility
If the Department determines that a member is no longer eligible for Medicaid, the  member  will  be  notified  by  the  Department  and  the  member  will  be

disenrolled from the BH I/DD Tailored Plan. The disenrollment effective date will be the last date of the member's Medicaid eligibility.
If  a  member  is  disenrolled  from  a  BH  I/DD  Tailored  Plan  solely  because  the member loses his or her eligibility for Medicaid for a period of two (2) months or less, the member will automatically be reenrolled in the BH I/DD Tailored Plan upon reenrollment in Medicaid. 13 1
(b) Change in Medicaid eligibility category
If the Department determines that a member is no longer eligible for Medicaid Managed Care because they become part of an excluded or temporarily excluded population as described in Section V.B.1.i.(iii)( c) the member will be notified by the Department and the Department will disenroll the member from the BH I/DD Tailored  Plan.  The  disenrollment  effective  date  will  be  the  date  when  the member's change in eligibility category was effective.
(c) Nursing facility long-term stays
A  member  with  a  nursing  facility  stay  that  exceeds  ninety  (90)  continuous calendar days will be disenrolled from the BH I/DD Tailored Plan on the first day of the next month following the ninetieth (90th) day of stay and receive services through NC Medicaid Direct. 14

ID: sec:doc:federal_regulation:42-CFR-438:438.8
Title: Medical loss ratio (MLR) standards
Section: 438.8
Policy: 42-CFR-438
Type: federal_regulation
Last revised: 2024-05-10
Federal Register cite: [81 FR 27853, May 6, 2016, as amended at 82 FR 39, Jan. 3, 2017; 85 FR 72840, Nov. 13, 2020; 89 FR 41272, May 10, 2024]
Citation link: [42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)

Content:
(a) Basic rule. The State must ensure, through its contracts starting on or after July 1, 2017, that each MCO, PIHP, and PAHP calculate and report a MLR in accordance with this section. For multi-year contracts that do not start in 2017, the State must require the MCO, PIHP, or PAHP to calculate and report a MLR for the rating period that begins in 2017.

(b) Definitions. As used in this section, the following terms have the indicated meanings:

Credibility adjustment means an adjustment to the MLR for a partially credible MCO, PIHP, or PAHP to account for a difference between the actual and target MLRs that may be due to random statistical variation.

Full credibility means a standard for which the experience of an MCO, PIHP, or PAHP is determined to be sufficient for the calculation of a MLR with a minimal chance that the difference between the actual and target medical loss ratio is not statistically significant. An MCO, PIHP, or PAHP that is assigned full credibility (or is fully credible) will not receive a credibility adjustment to its MLR.

Member months mean the number of months an enrollee or a group of enrollees is covered by an MCO, PIHP, or PAHP over a specified time period, such as a year.

MLR reporting year means a period of 12 months consistent with the rating period selected by the State.

No credibility means a standard for which the experience of an MCO, PIHP, or PAHP is determined to be insufficient for the calculation of a MLR. An MCO, PIHP, or PAHP that is assigned no credibility (or is non-credible) will not be measured against any MLR requirements.

Non-claims costs means those expenses for administrative services that are not: Incurred claims (as defined in paragraph (e)(2) of this section); expenditures on activities that improve health care quality (as defined in paragraph (e)(3) of this section); or licensing and regulatory fees, or Federal and State taxes (as defined in paragraph (f)(2) of this section).

Partial credibility means a standard for which the experience of an MCO, PIHP, or PAHP is determined to be sufficient for the calculation of a MLR but with a non-negligible chance that the difference between the actual and target medical loss ratios is statistically significant. An MCO, PIHP, or PAHP that is assigned partial credibility (or is partially credible) will receive a credibility adjustment to its MLR.

The MLR experienced for each MCO, PIHP, or PAHP in a MLR reporting year is the ratio of the numerator (as defined in paragraph (e) of this section) to the denominator (as defined in paragraph (f) of this section). A MLR may be increased by a credibility adjustment, in accordance with paragraph (h) of this section.

(e) Numerator —(1) Required elements. The numerator of an MCO's, PIHP's, or PAHP's MLR for a MLR reporting year is the sum of the MCO's, PIHP's, or PAHP's incurred claims (as defined in (e)(2) of this section); the MCO's, PIHP's, or PAHP's expenditures for activities that improve health care quality (as defined in paragraph (e)(3) of this section); and fraud prevention activities (as defined in paragraph (e)(4) of this section).

(C) Withholds from payments made to network providers.

(E) Claims payments recoveries received as a result of subrogation.

(F) Incurred but not reported claims based on past experience, and modified to reflect current conditions, such as changes in exposure or claim frequency or severity.

(G) Changes in other claims-related reserves.

(H) Reserves for contingent benefits and the medical claim portion of lawsuits.

(ii) Amounts that must be deducted from incurred claims include the following:

(B) The amount of claims payments recovered through fraud reduction efforts, not to exceed the amount of fraud reduction expenses. The amount of fraud reduction expenses must not include activities specified in paragraph (e)(4) of this section.

(C) The amount of payments made to providers under State directed payments described in § 438.6(c).

per_question.question: When does NC Medicaid pay for CAR-T cell treatment? What specific criteria have to be met?
per_question.agent_answer:
NC Medicaid pays for CAR-T cell therapy when it is **medically necessary** and all of the policy’s specific coverage conditions are met under current Clinical Coverage Policy 11A-17, effective April 1, 2025. [Policy 11A-17 § 3.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment) [Policy 11A-17 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

## Specific criteria that must be met

NC Medicaid covers CAR-T cell therapy only if **all** of the following are true: [Policy 11A-17 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

- The CAR-T product has **U.S. FDA approval**. [Policy 11A-17 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)
- It is used **within the FDA-approved guidelines** for:
  - indications and usage, [Policy 11A-17 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)
  - dosage and administration, [Policy 11A-17 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)
  - dosage forms and strengths, and [Policy 11A-17 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)
  - warnings and precautions. [Policy 11A-17 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)
- The therapy is given at a **certified or authorized treatment center**. [Policy 11A-17 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)
- If the product is subject to a **REMS** program, the treatment center must be **enrolled in the REMS**, and providers must be **trained to manage cytokine release syndrome and neurologic toxicities**. [Policy 11A-17 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

In addition, the usual Medicaid medical-necessity standards in this policy must be met: the service must be **individualized, specific, and consistent with the beneficiary’s symptoms or confirmed diagnosis**, **not in excess of the beneficiary’s needs**, **safely furnished**, and there must be **no equally effective and more conservative or less costly treatment available statewide**; it also cannot be furnished primarily for the convenience of the beneficiary, caretaker, or provider. [Policy 11A-17 § 3.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

The policy says there are **no additional Medicaid-specific covered criteria** beyond those listed above. [Policy 11A-17 § 3.2.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

## Situations where NC Medicaid will not pay

NC Medicaid does **not** cover CAR-T cell therapy if **any one** of these applies: [Policy 11A-17 § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

- the CAR-T product is **not FDA approved**; [Policy 11A-17 § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)
- it is being given **outside FDA guidelines** for indications and usage, dosage and administration, or dosage forms and strengths; [Policy 11A-17 § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)
- a REMS-required therapy is given at a facility **not enrolled in that REMS program**; [Policy 11A-17 § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)
- the beneficiary previously received **another CAR-T therapy** and the requested treatment is a **repeat treatment**; [Policy 11A-17 § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)
- the beneficiary’s **psychosocial history limits ability to comply** with pre- and post-infusion care; or [Policy 11A-17 § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)
- there is current beneficiary or caretaker **non-compliance** making adherence to a disciplined medical regimen improbable. [Policy 11A-17 § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

NC Medicaid also does **not** cover a **concurrent rescue transplant with infusion of any CAR-T therapy**, because the policy considers that experimental. [Policy 11A-17 § 4.2.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

## Prior approval

CAR-T cell therapy requires **prior approval before it is rendered**. [Policy 11A-17 § 5.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

## Bottom line

For NC Medicaid to pay, the CAR-T treatment must be **medically necessary**, **FDA-approved**, used **exactly within FDA-approved parameters**, delivered at the right **certified/authorized and REMS-compliant center**, and the patient must be able to comply with the required care plan. [Policy 11A-17 § 3.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment) [Policy 11A-17 § 3.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment) [Policy 11A-17 § 4.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

If you want, I can also pull out the **prior-authorization submission requirements** or help compare this policy to a specific beneficiary’s diagnosis and treatment plan.

All claims are directly supported by the Evidence block. Citations are precise and section-level throughout. The answer is comprehensive, well-organized, and would be fully acceptable to a Medicaid policy expert.

per_question.question: Up to what age can children on Medicaid receive fluoride varnish from their physician, and what oral screening has to accompany it?
per_question.agent_answer:
Children can receive physician-applied fluoride varnish under this policy from tooth eruption until age 3½.[Policy 1A-23 § 3.2.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1a-23-physician-fluoride-varnish-services/download?attachment) The policy says Medicaid covers a total of six oral screening packages during that period.[Policy 1A-23 § 3.2.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1a-23-physician-fluoride-varnish-services/download?attachment)

The oral screening package that accompanies the varnish must include an examination/oral evaluation, preventive oral health and dietary counseling, and the application of fluoride varnish.[Policy 1A-23 § 3.2.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1a-23-physician-fluoride-varnish-services/download?attachment) More specifically, the oral screening must include early caries screening and detection of notable findings in the mouth using a dental mirror and directed light, plus counseling and educational materials on oral hygiene and nutrition for children.[Policy 1A-23 § 7.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1a-23-physician-fluoride-varnish-services/download?attachment)

The policy also requires documentation of the oral evaluation and any notable findings, preventive oral health and dietary counseling with the primary caregiver, application of fluoride varnish, and referral to a dentist if appropriate.[Policy 1A-23 § 7.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1a-23-physician-fluoride-varnish-services/download?attachment)

This policy was amended effective April 1, 2023, with updated template language in the latest change notice.[Policy 1A-23 Revision — 2023-04-15](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1a-23-physician-fluoride-varnish-services/download?attachment)

The documentation requirements are accurately listed. All claims are supported by the Evidence block. Citations are precise, referencing specific section numbers (§3.2.2 and §7.2). The amendment date of April 1, 2023 is confirmed in the evidence. No hallucinations detected.

Content:
Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment (EPSDT) is a federal Medicaid requirement that requires the state Medicaid agency to cover services, products, or procedures for Medicaid beneficiary under 21 years of age if the service is medically necessary health care to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition [health problem] identified through a screening examination (includes any evaluation by a physician or other licensed practitioner).
This means EPSDT covers most of the medical or remedial care a child needs to improve or maintain his or her health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.
Medically necessary services will be provided in the most economic mode, as long as the treatment made available is similarly efficacious to the service requested by the beneficiary's physician, therapist, or other licensed practitioner; the determination process does not delay the delivery of the needed service; and the determination does not limit the beneficiary's right to a free choice of providers.
EPSDT does not require the state Medicaid agency to provide any service, product or procedure:
that is unsafe, ineffective, or experimental or investigational.
that is not medical in nature or not generally recognized as an accepted method of medical practice or treatment.
Service limitations on scope, amount, duration, frequency, location of service, and other specific criteria described in clinical coverage policies may be exceeded or may not apply as long as the provider's documentation shows that the requested service is medically necessary 'to correct or ameliorate a defect, physical or mental illness, or a condition' [health problem]; that is, provider documentation shows how the service, product, or procedure meets all EPSDT criteria, including to correct or improve or maintain the beneficiary's health in the best condition possible, compensate for a health problem, prevent it from worsening, or prevent the development of additional health problems.

Early caries screening and detection of notable findings (obvious pathology of hard and soft tissues) in the oral cavity using a dental mirror and directed light.
Counseling and educational materials on good oral hygiene practices and nutrition for children.
c.
Prescribing a fluoride supplement, if indicated, per the guidelines of the American Association of Pediatrics:
https://publications.aap.org/pediatrics/article/146/6/e2020034637/33536/FluorideUse-in-Caries-Prevention-in-the-Primary?autologincheck=redirected
Note: It is critical to have the beneficiary's drinking water tested for fluoride content if the level of fluoride in the source of drinking water is unknown. Providers shall refer the beneficiary to a dentist for continued treatment at the appropriate age based on the beneficiary's need for dental services.
Application of the fluoride varnish to all erupted primary teeth, beginning at tooth eruption until the beneficiary is 3½ years of age.
Documentation in the beneficiary's health record shall include all of the following:
an oral evaluation and any notable findings;
preventive oral health and dietary counseling with the primary caregiver;
application of fluoride varnish; and
referral to a dentist, if appropriate.

per_question.question: An NC Innovations participant's needs cost more than their individual base budget. Can they request services beyond the budget, and what recourse do they have if they think the budget can't meet their needs?
per_question.agent_answer:
Yes. An NC Innovations participant may request services that cost more than the participant’s base budget if they believe their needs cannot be met within that base budget, and the base budget is not a binding cap on what may be requested or authorized. If the LME/MCO or Utilization Management determines the requested services are medically necessary, those services must be authorized even if they exceed the base budget.

## What they can request

The policy says a participant whose needs cannot be met within the base budget may request services in excess of that budget.

The policy also says no change in the budget amount is required in order to approve services above the budget.

## Why the budget is not absolute

The policy describes the individual budget as only one measure of likely current needs and says it is not a binding limit on funding for any period of time.

It also states that SIS results and the base budget are guidelines, not binding limits, and medically necessary services are to be authorized regardless of the base budget.

## What recourse they have if the budget will not meet their needs

If the participant has a level change that increases the budget, the increase can take effect 60 calendar days from the date on the notice letter, and during that period the participant can work with the planning team to update the ISP for increased services, which the Care Coordinator submits for UM approval.

If the participant requests authorization for services and the request is denied, the LME/MCO must notify the participant of the reasons for the decision and how to appeal.

The policy also says the participant must be told how to file a grievance regarding the base budget if they wish to do so.

## Important limit

The policy also contains an overall waiver cost limit of $135,000 for combined base-budget and non-base-budget services, with a stated exception for certain beneficiaries using Supported Living Level III who live independently, receive Supported Living Level III, and require 24-hour support.

## Current-version note

The 8P policy text I relied on is tied to a later revision history, and the amendment record identifies the authoritative document as the 2016-11-01 revision for Policy 8P. [unverified: the amendment record identifies the authoritative document as the 2016-11-01 revision for Policy 8P.]

The federal section surfaced in the frame, 42 CFR § 435.121, addresses Medicaid eligibility rules in states using more restrictive SSI-related requirements and does not provide the Innovations budget-override rule itself.

If you want, I can next pull together a short appeal/grievance roadmap for an Innovations participant who has been told “the budget won’t allow it.”

---

- [Policy 8P § Changes within the Individual Budget Tool](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8-p-north-carolina-innovations/download?attachment)

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8P:_s564
Title: Category Assignment and Individual Budget Changes
Policy: 8P
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Clinical Coverage Policy 8-P, North Carolina Innovations](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8-p-north-carolina-innovations/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched category.
Content:
A Level is assigned every person on the NC Innovations Waiver. This level is based on the Support Intensity Scale ('SIS') which is the assessment instrument used to measure individual support needs.
The SIS scores are uploaded to SIS On-line with AAIDD.  Within 15 calendar days of receiving notice that the SIS has been uploaded, NC Medicaid, or their designee, applies the algorithm and assigns an initial level and individual budget.  If a SIS is updated, the results of the SIS may indicate a change in the level of support needs.  This may result in a new Individual Budget Tool Level and base budget being assigned. Within thirty (30) calendar days of a SIS being performed and NC Medicaid, or their designee's notification, NC Medicaid, or their designee will determine if there has been a Level change and the LME/MCO will notify the beneficiary in writing within 15 days of receiving notice from NC Medicaid, or their designee.  The beneficiary will also be notified if there is not a Level change.  A Level change may not always result in a change in the beneficiary's base budget, but the beneficiary will always be notified if there is a Level change and budget change.
If the beneficiary's level change has resulted in an increase in budget, that budget increase can take effect sixty (60) calendar days from the date on the letter. During that sixty (60) calendar day period, the individual can develop an update to his/her Individual Support Plan ('ISP') with the planning team allowing for the increased services, if they choose. The Care Coordinator will submit an updated ISP to UM for approval. If the beneficiary's Level change has resulted in a decrease in budget, the budget decrease will take effect at the end of the individual's most recently approved Annual ISP. No currently authorized services will be reduced as a result of the budget change. The letters notifying the individual of the decrease in budget will notify the individual of the following:
He or she may request services that cost in excess of his or her base budget if he or she believes his or her needs cannot be met within his or her base budget; and
The results of the SIS and the base budget are guidelines that do not constitute a binding limit on the amount of services that may be requested or authorized, and if the LME/MCO determines services to be medically necessary, they will be authorized, regardless of the base budget.
If any request for authorization of services is denied, the LME/MCO will notify the individual of the reasons for the decision and how to appeal
How to file a grievance regarding the base budget if he or she wishes to do so.

Sometimes, an individual's support needs may not be met in his or her assigned level base budget.  If Utilization Management determines requested services to be medically necessary, they will be authorized.
There are a variety of ways for a beneficiary's base budget to be modified. However, no change in the amount of the budget is needed in order to approve services in excess of the budget.

Reason: Matched documentation.
Content:
Medicaid
Clinical Coverage Policy No: 8-P
Amended Date: April 1, 2023
Monitoring takes place in all service settings and on a schedule outlined in the ISP.
The Care Coordinator is responsible for monitoring the ISP, and reviews goals at a minimum frequency based on the target date assigned to each goal. Goals may be, and often are, reviewed more frequently, based on the needs of the beneficiary.  The Care Coordinator also maintains close contact with the beneficiary, the legally responsible person or parent or guardian (if applicable), providers, and other members of the person-centered planning team, noting any recommended revisions needed.  This ensures that changes are noted, and updates are effectuated in a timely manner.
Monitoring methods also consist of contacts (face-to-face and telephone calls) with other members of the ISP team and review of service documentation. A standard monitoring checklist is used to ensure that the following issues are monitored:
Verification that services are provided as outlined in the ISP;
The beneficiary has access to services;
Identification of any problems that may arise;
The services meet the needs of the beneficiary;
The back-up staffing plans are documented;
Issues of health and welfare (rights restrictions, medical care, abuse, neglect or exploitation, behavior support plan) are addressed;
That the beneficiary has been offered a free choice of providers; and
That non-waiver services needs have been addressed.
Care Coordinator monitoring occurs monthly and consists of the following:
A beneficiary that is new to the waiver receives face-to-face visits for the first six months and then on a schedule agreed to by the ISP team thereafter, no less than quarterly, to meet their health and safety needs;
A beneficiary whose services are provided by guardians and relatives living in the home of the beneficiary receives monthly face-to-face monitoring visits;
A beneficiary who lives in residential programs receives face-to-face monitoring visits monthly;
A beneficiary who chooses the individual family-directed service option receives face-to-face monitoring visits monthly;
For the months that the beneficiary does not receive face-to-face monitoring, the Care Coordinator has telephone contact with the beneficiary to ensure that there are no issues that need to be addressed;
At least one service is utilized monthly, per waiver eligibility requirements;
NC Innovations services utilized do not exceed authorization.  If there is an emergency, the Care Coordinator shall ensure that beneficiary's needs are met and ensure that any updates to the LOC and ISP, based upon the changes in needs of the beneficiary, are processed in a timely manner; and
Home and Community Based Services (HCBS) rules are met. Any concerns noted by the Care Coordinator regarding HCBS (such as privacy, restriction
of rights, access to food) must be reported to the PIHP. Any restrictions to HCBS must be addressed in the ISP.

Title: Individuals in States using more restrictive requirements for Medicaid than the SSI requirements
Section: 435.121
Policy: 42-CFR-435
Type: federal_regulation
Last revised: 2013-07-15
Federal Register cite: [58 FR 4926, Jan. 19, 1993, as amended at 78 FR 42302, July 15, 2013]
Citation link: [42 CFR Part 435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-435)
Reason: Matched cover.
Content:
(a) Basic eligibility group requirements. (1) If the agency does not provide Medicaid under § 435.120 to aged, blind, and disabled individuals who are SSI beneficiaries, the agency must provide Medicaid to aged, blind, and disabled individuals who meet eligibility requirements that are specified in this section.

(2) Except to the extent provided in paragraph (a)(3) of this section, the agency may elect to apply more restrictive eligibility requirements to the aged, blind, and disabled that are more restrictive than those of the SSI program. The more restrictive requirements may be no more restrictive than those requirements contained in the State's Medicaid plan in effect on January 1, 1972. If any of the State's 1972 Medicaid plan requirements were more liberal than of the SSI program, the State must use the SSI requirement instead of the more liberal requirements, except to the extent the State elects to use more liberal criteria under § 435.601.

(3) The agency must not apply a more restrictive requirement under the provisions of paragraph (a)(2) of this section if:

(i) The requirement conflicts with the requirements of section 1924 of the Act, which governs the eligibility and post-eligibility treatment of income and resources of institutionalized individuals with community spouses;

(ii) The requirement conflicts with a more liberal requirement which the agency has elected to use under § 435.601; or

(iii) The more restrictive requirement conflicts with a more liberal requirement the State has elected to use under § 435.234(c) in determining eligibility for State supplementary payments.

(b) Mandatory coverage. If the agency chooses to apply more restrictive requirements than SSI to aged, blind, or disabled individuals, it must provide Medicaid to:

(1) Individuals who meet the requirements of section 1619(b)(3) of the Act even though they may not continue to meet the requirements of this section; and

(2) Qualified Medicare beneficiaries described in section 1905(p) of the Act and qualified working disabled individuals described in section 1905(s) of the Act without consideration of the more restrictive eligibility requirements specified in this section.

(3) Individuals who:

(i) Qualify for benefits under section 1619(a) or are in eligibility status under section 1619(b)(1) of the Act as determined by SSA; and

(ii) Were eligible for Medicaid under the more restrictive criteria in the State's approved Medicaid plan in the reference month—the month immediately preceding the first month in which they became eligible under section 1619(a) or (b)(1) of the Act. “Were eligible for Medicaid” means that individuals were issued Medicaid cards by the State for the reference month. Under this provision, the reference month for determining Medicaid eligibility for all individuals under section 1619 of the Act is the month immediately preceding the first month of the most recent period of eligibility under section 1619 of the Act.

(c) Group composition. The agency may apply more restrictive requirements only to the aged, to the blind, to the disabled, or to any combination of these groups. For example, the agency may apply more restrictive requirements to the aged and disabled under this provision and provide Medicaid to all blind individuals who are SSI beneficiaries.

(d) Nonfinancial conditions. The agency may apply more restrictive requirements that are nonfinancial conditions of eligibility. For example, the agency may use a more restrictive definition of disability or may limit eligibility of the disabled to individuals age 18 and older, or both. If the agency limits eligibility of disabled individuals to individuals age 18 or older, it must provide Medicaid to individuals under age 18 who receive SSI benefits and who would be eligible to receive AFDC under the State's approved plan if they did not receive SSI. If the agency imposed an age limit for disabled individuals under its 1972 approved State plan but does not use that limit, it must apply the same nonfinancial requirement to individuals under age 18 that it applies to disabled individuals age 18 and older.

(e) Financial conditions. (1) The agency may apply more restrictive requirements that are financial conditions of eligibility.

(2) Any income eligibility standards that the agency applies must:

(i) Equal the income standard (or Federal Benefit Rate (FBR)) that would be used under SSI based on an individual's living arrangement; or

(ii) Be a more restrictive standard which is no more restrictive than that under the approved State's January 1, 1972 Medicaid plan.

(3) If the categorically needy income standard established under paragraph (e)(2) of this section is less than the optional categorically needy standard established under § 435.230, the agency must provide Medicaid to all aged, blind, and disabled individuals who have income equal to or below the higher standard.

(4) In a State that does not have a medically needy program that covers aged, blind, and disabled individuals, the agency must allow individuals to deduct from income incurred medical and remedial expenses (that is, spend down) to become eligible under this section. However, individuals with income above the categorically needy standards may only spend down to the standard selected by the State under paragraph (e)(2) of this section which applies to the individual's living arrangement.

(5) In a State that elects to provide medically needy coverage to aged, blind, and disabled individuals, the agency must allow individuals to deduct from income incurred medical and remedial care expenses (spend down) to become categorically needy when they are SSI beneficiaries (including individuals deemed to be SSI beneficiaries under §§ 435.135, 435.137, and 435.138), eligible spouses of SSI beneficiaries, State supplement beneficiaries, and individuals who are eligible for a supplement but who do not receive supplementary payments. Title: NC Medicaid North Carolina Innovations

Reason: Matched cover.
Content:
Clinical Coverage Policy No: 8-P
Amended Date: April 1, 2023
All Requests for Community Living and Supports require prior approval by the PIHP:
Requests for up to 12 hours daily may be authorized for the entire plan year.
Requests for up to 16 hours daily may be authorized for a six-month timeframe, within the plan year.
Requests for more than 16 hours daily are authorized for up to a 90-day period within the plan year. In situations requiring an authorization beyond the initial 90-day period, the PIHP shall approve such authorization based on review of Medical Necessity. The treatment team should meet to review individuals' status and identify sustainable supports, if available and information from the meeting should be included in the individual's ISP.  Review of other options should include options within the Innovations Waiver, as well as options outside of the Innovations waiver such as Medicaid State Plan Services.
The service may be provided in the home or community. The involvement of unpaid supports in the generalization of the service is an important aspect to ensure that achieved goals are practiced and maintained.  Services may be allowed in the private home of the provider or staff of an Employer of Record at the discretion and agreement of the support team and when consistent with the ISP goals. If services are provided in the primary residence of the provider or staff of the employer of record, the Health and Safety Checklist must be completed before service begins and every six months thereafter.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8P:_s564
Title: Category Assignment and Individual Budget Changes
Policy: 8P
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2016-11-01
Citation link: [Clinical Coverage Policy 8-P, North Carolina Innovations](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8-p-north-carolina-innovations/download?attachment)

Content:
A Level is assigned every person on the NC Innovations Waiver. This level is based on the Support Intensity Scale ('SIS') which is the assessment instrument used to measure individual support needs.
The SIS scores are uploaded to SIS On-line with AAIDD.  Within 15 calendar days of receiving notice that the SIS has been uploaded, NC Medicaid, or their designee, applies the algorithm and assigns an initial level and individual budget.  If a SIS is updated, the results of the SIS may indicate a change in the level of support needs.  This may result in a new Individual Budget Tool Level and base budget being assigned. Within thirty (30) calendar days of a SIS being performed and NC Medicaid, or their designee's notification, NC Medicaid, or their designee will determine if there has been a Level change and the LME/MCO will notify the beneficiary in writing within 15 days of receiving notice from NC Medicaid, or their designee.  The beneficiary will also be notified if there is not a Level change.  A Level change may not always result in a change in the beneficiary's base budget, but the beneficiary will always be notified if there is a Level change and budget change.
If the beneficiary's level change has resulted in an increase in budget, that budget increase can take effect sixty (60) calendar days from the date on the letter. During that sixty (60) calendar day period, the individual can develop an update to his/her Individual Support Plan ('ISP') with the planning team allowing for the increased services, if they choose. The Care Coordinator will submit an updated ISP to UM for approval. If the beneficiary's Level change has resulted in a decrease in budget, the budget decrease will take effect at the end of the individual's most recently approved Annual ISP. No currently authorized services will be reduced as a result of the budget change. The letters notifying the individual of the decrease in budget will notify the individual of the following:
He or she may request services that cost in excess of his or her base budget if he or she believes his or her needs cannot be met within his or her base budget; and
The results of the SIS and the base budget are guidelines that do not constitute a binding limit on the amount of services that may be requested or authorized, and if the LME/MCO determines services to be medically necessary, they will be authorized, regardless of the base budget.
If any request for authorization of services is denied, the LME/MCO will notify the individual of the reasons for the decision and how to appeal
How to file a grievance regarding the base budget if he or she wishes to do so.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:8P:_s565
Title: Changes within the Individual Budget Tool
Policy: 8P
Type: clinical_policy
Effective: 2016-11-01
Citation link: [Clinical Coverage Policy 8-P, North Carolina Innovations](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8-p-north-carolina-innovations/download?attachment)

Content:
Sometimes, an individual's support needs may not be met in his or her assigned level base budget.  If Utilization Management determines requested services to be medically necessary, they will be authorized.
There are a variety of ways for a beneficiary's base budget to be modified. However, no change in the amount of the budget is needed in order to approve services in excess of the budget.

Title: Components of the Individual Budgeting Tool

Content:
The Individual Budget is only one measure of a beneficiary's likely current needs and is not a binding limit on the amount of funding for any period of time. The Individual Budget is reviewed no less frequently than annually by the PIHP. The Individual Budget includes only Base Budget Services. NonBase Budget services are not included. Base Budget services are the core habilitation and support services in the waiver. Non-Base Budget services are preventative services, and equipment. Combined these services may not total more than the $135,000 cost limit within the waiver unless the follow criteria is met:
An individual may exceed the $135,000 waiver limit, to ensure health, safety and wellbeing, if the following criteria is met:
Beneficiaries utilizing Supported Living Level III:
lives independently without his or her family in a home that s/he owns, rents or leases, and
receives Supported Living Level III, and
requires 24 hour support.

ID: sec:doc:federal_regulation:42-CFR-435:435.121
Title: Individuals in States using more restrictive requirements for Medicaid than the SSI requirements
Section: 435.121
Policy: 42-CFR-435
Type: federal_regulation
Last revised: 2013-07-15
Federal Register cite: [58 FR 4926, Jan. 19, 1993, as amended at 78 FR 42302, July 15, 2013]
Citation link: [42 CFR Part 435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-435)

Content:
(a) Basic eligibility group requirements. (1) If the agency does not provide Medicaid under § 435.120 to aged, blind, and disabled individuals who are SSI beneficiaries, the agency must provide Medicaid to aged, blind, and disabled individuals who meet eligibility requirements that are specified in this section.

(2) Except to the extent provided in paragraph (a)(3) of this section, the agency may elect to apply more restrictive eligibility requirements to the aged, blind, and disabled that are more restrictive than those of the SSI program. The more restrictive requirements may be no more restrictive than those requirements contained in the State's Medicaid plan in effect on January 1, 1972. If any of the State's 1972 Medicaid plan requirements were more liberal than of the SSI program, the State must use the SSI requirement instead of the more liberal requirements, except to the extent the State elects to use more liberal criteria under § 435.601.

(3) The agency must not apply a more restrictive requirement under the provisions of paragraph (a)(2) of this section if:

(i) The requirement conflicts with the requirements of section 1924 of the Act, which governs the eligibility and post-eligibility treatment of income and resources of institutionalized individuals with community spouses;

(ii) The requirement conflicts with a more liberal requirement which the agency has elected to use under § 435.601; or

(iii) The more restrictive requirement conflicts with a more liberal requirement the State has elected to use under § 435.234(c) in determining eligibility for State supplementary payments.

(b) Mandatory coverage. If the agency chooses to apply more restrictive requirements than SSI to aged, blind, or disabled individuals, it must provide Medicaid to:

(1) Individuals who meet the requirements of section 1619(b)(3) of the Act even though they may not continue to meet the requirements of this section; and

(2) Qualified Medicare beneficiaries described in section 1905(p) of the Act and qualified working disabled individuals described in section 1905(s) of the Act without consideration of the more restrictive eligibility requirements specified in this section.

(3) Individuals who:

(i) Qualify for benefits under section 1619(a) or are in eligibility status under section 1619(b)(1) of the Act as determined by SSA; and

(ii) Were eligible for Medicaid under the more restrictive criteria in the State's approved Medicaid plan in the reference month—the month immediately preceding the first month in which they became eligible under section 1619(a) or (b)(1) of the Act. “Were eligible for Medicaid” means that individuals were issued Medicaid cards by the State for the reference month. Under this provision, the reference month for determining Medicaid eligibility for all individuals under section 1619 of the Act is the month immediately preceding the first month of the most recent period of eligibility under section 1619 of the Act.

(c) Group composition. The agency may apply more restrictive requirements only to the aged, to the blind, to the disabled, or to any combination of these groups. For example, the agency may apply more restrictive requirements to the aged and disabled under this provision and provide Medicaid to all blind individuals who are SSI beneficiaries.

(d) Nonfinancial conditions. The agency may apply more restrictive requirements that are nonfinancial conditions of eligibility. For example, the agency may use a more restrictive definition of disability or may limit eligibility of the disabled to individuals age 18 and older, or both. If the agency limits eligibility of disabled individuals to individuals age 18 or older, it must provide Medicaid to individuals under age 18 who receive SSI benefits and who would be eligible to receive AFDC under the State's approved plan if they did not receive SSI. If the agency imposed an age limit for disabled individuals under its 1972 approved State plan but does not use that limit, it must apply the same nonfinancial requirement to individuals under age 18 that it applies to disabled individuals age 18 and older.

(e) Financial conditions. (1) The agency may apply more restrictive requirements that are financial conditions of eligibility.

(2) Any income eligibility standards that the agency applies must:

(i) Equal the income standard (or Federal Benefit Rate (FBR)) that would be used under SSI based on an individual's living arrangement; or

(ii) Be a more restrictive standard which is no more restrictive than that under the approved State's January 1, 1972 Medicaid plan.

(3) If the categorically needy income standard established under paragraph (e)(2) of this section is less than the optional categorically needy standard established under § 435.230, the agency must provide Medicaid to all aged, blind, and disabled individuals who have income equal to or below the higher standard.

(4) In a State that does not have a medically needy program that covers aged, blind, and disabled individuals, the agency must allow individuals to deduct from income incurred medical and remedial expenses (that is, spend down) to become eligible under this section. However, individuals with income above the categorically needy standards may only spend down to the standard selected by the State under paragraph (e)(2) of this section which applies to the individual's living arrangement.

(5) In a State that elects to provide medically needy coverage to aged, blind, and disabled individuals, the agency must allow individuals to deduct from income incurred medical and remedial care expenses (spend down) to become categorically needy when they are SSI beneficiaries (including individuals deemed to be SSI beneficiaries under §§ 435.135, 435.137, and 435.138), eligible spouses of SSI beneficiaries, State supplement beneficiaries, and individuals who are eligible for a supplement but who do not receive supplementary payments. per_question.question: What does it take to become a certified HIV case management provider for NC Medicaid, and what circumstances can lead to a provider losing that certification?
per_question.agent_answer:
To become a certified HIV case management provider for NC Medicaid, an agency must obtain certification from NC Medicaid or its designated contractor before it can be enrolled as an HIV Case Management provider, and it must satisfy both agency-level and staffing requirements under Clinical Coverage Policy 12B. The current policy was later revised on August 15, 2023, but that change notice says the update was template language tied to the Health Choice transition, not a substantive rewrite of these certification standards. [Policy 12B § 6.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment) [Policy 12B Change Notice 2023-08-15](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

## What it takes to become certified

An eligible provider can be an agency such as a home health agency, home care agency, hospice, health department, hospital, department of social services, federally qualified health clinic, rural health clinic, community-based organization, or local management entity. [Policy 12B § 6.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

The agency must have a documented successful record of three years providing or managing HIV case management programs. [Policy 12B § 6.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

The agency must ensure that its HIV case managers meet the case manager qualification standards and that its supervisors meet the supervisor qualification standards. [Policy 12B § 6.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

Each physical site must be separately enrolled with NC Medicaid as an HIV case management provider site. [Policy 12B § 6.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

The agency must comply with applicable state and federal Medicaid participation laws, maintain certification, comply with initial and ongoing certification processes, maintain a quality improvement process for monitoring case management records, allow NC Medicaid or its contractor to review beneficiary, operational, and financial records, and report proposed ownership/name/address/phone changes within 30 calendar days and actual changes within five business days. [Policy 12B § 6.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

Within one year after Medicaid enrollment, the provider must achieve national accreditation from at least one listed accrediting body: ACHC, CARF, CHAP, COA, PHAB, The Joint Commission, or URAC. [Policy 12B § 6.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

A provider is ineligible for certification if it has previously been decertified as an HIV case management provider, if its provider number was suspended because of Program Integrity sanctions, or if it has failed to repay money owed to the North Carolina Medicaid program. [Policy 12B § 6.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

The provider is also responsible for verifying staff qualifications and credentials before hiring and maintaining proof that staff continue to meet policy requirements. [Policy 12B § 6.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

### Staffing qualifications

An HIV case manager must meet one of several education/license pathways, such as a qualifying master’s degree in a human services field, a BSW, certain other bachelor’s-degree paths with specified coursework or experience, or certain North Carolina licenses with two years of human services experience. In addition, the case manager must have two years of case management experience and must possess or acquire a clinical understanding of HIV documented in the personnel file. [Policy 12B § 6.1.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

Required case management experience must include functions such as intake, assessment, reassessment, care planning, case coordination, case conferencing, care plan implementation, referral, linkage and resource development, crisis intervention, monitoring and follow-up, and discharge or termination. [Policy 12B § 6.1.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

Case managers must also demonstrate specified knowledge and skills, including basic HIV knowledge, communication, information gathering and synthesis, resource identification, assessment-related skills, cultural sensitivity, judgment, and accurate documentation. The policy requires documented proof of basic HIV knowledge within one year of hire. [Policy 12B § 6.1.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

A supervisor must meet one of the listed degree/licensure-and-experience pathways and, in addition, must have three years of case management experience. [Policy 12B § 6.1.4](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

Supervisor experience must cover the same broad case-management functions, and the supervisor must provide regularly scheduled supervision addressing both clinical and professional performance. Each beneficiary record must show supervisory review at least every four weeks, with billing checked against progress notes. [Policy 12B § 6.1.5](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

### Training requirements

All HIV case managers and supervisors must complete North Carolina state-sponsored basic training within 90 days of employment, and before any billed case management units. Providers must keep completion certificates. [Policy 12B § 6.1.7.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

All HIV case managers and supervisors must also complete 12 hours of HIV case management continuing education each year, with 6 of those hours clinically oriented. [Policy 12B § 6.1.7.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

### Application / certification process

Initial certification is valid for one year, and the provider must submit a complete and signed application including the administrative, case management, and human resource information required by the policy. [Policy 12B § 6.2.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

The recertification materials help show what NC Medicaid expects the provider to document, including one physical location per application, a signed checklist, agency demographics, all case managers and supervisors with dates of employment, all counties served, services offered, operating hours, an emergency after-hours plan, accreditation information, satisfaction-survey practices, and counts of Medicaid and Ryan White clients. [dma-3157 HIV Case Management Provider Recertification Application Checklist](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/dma-3157.pdf) [dma-3158 HIV Case Management Provider Recertification Application](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/dma-3158.pdf)

## What can cause a provider to lose certification

NC Medicaid or its designated contractor certifies qualified providers and may decertify agencies that fail to provide services according to professionally recognized standards and the policy. [Policy 12B § 6.2.2](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

Policy 12B says a provider may be decertified and disenrolled if any listed condition is substantiated, including failure to provide core service components, fraudulent billing, owner felony conviction, failure to submit or implement a required written plan of correction within 30 calendar days, falsification of records, violation of beneficiary confidentiality, employing staff who do not meet qualification standards, failure to complete mandatory basic training within 90 days, failure to obtain required CEUs, failure to provide needed supervision, failure to submit required documentation on time, failure to maintain documentation sufficient to support billing, failure to implement and enforce a quality improvement program, failure to timely notify NC Medicaid or the contractor of key agency changes, failure to comply with applicable federal and state laws and Medicaid policies, failure to enroll any beneficiaries within four months of certification, or failure to achieve or maintain certification requirements. [Policy 12B § 6.2.5](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

If NC Medicaid or its designated agent notifies an enrolled provider that it is no longer certified to provide HIV case management services, the provider may request reconsideration review under 10A NCAC 22F.0402. [Policy 12B § 6.2.5](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

## Practical bottom line

In short, certification requires an agency with a three-year successful HIV case management track record, qualified case managers and supervisors, required training, separate site enrollment, compliance systems, record-review access for NC Medicaid, timely reporting of business changes, and national accreditation within one year of Medicaid enrollment. [Policy 12B § 6.2.1](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment) [Policy 12B § 6.2.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

A provider can lose certification for both integrity problems and operational noncompliance, especially inadequate staffing qualifications, missing training or CEUs, documentation and billing failures, confidentiality breaches, failure to correct deficiencies, or failure to maintain certification standards. [Policy 12B § 6.2.5](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.5
Title: 6.1.5 Case Management Supervisor's Experience
Section: 6.1.5
Policy: 12B
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Case Management](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched documentation.
Content:
Case management experience must encompass the functions of intake, assessment, reassessment, care planning, case coordination, case conferencing, care plan implementation, referral, linkage and resource development, crisis intervention, monitoring and follow -up of services provided and discharge or termination.
Knowledge, Skills and Abilities
In addition to those listed for the CM, the case management supervisor must possess and demonstrate the following knowledge, skills and abilities:
Ability to direct and evaluate the scope and quality of case management services;
Knowledgeable in case management principals, procedures and practices;
Ability to conduct detailed analytical evaluations and studies, and prepare related reports and recommendations; and
Apply professional level of knowledge of federal and state assistance programs for HIV positive population.
The provider shall identify the HIV CM program supervisor within the organization. The supervisor is to provide supervision that addresses both the clinical and professional aspects of the CM's job performance. This is defined as providing regularly scheduled assistance by a qualified professional to a staff member who is working directly with beneficiaries.
The purpose of clinical supervision is to ensure that each beneficiary receives case management services which are consistent with accepted standards of practice and the needs of the beneficiary and care plan.
Documentation of supervisory review of CM's caseload and proper utilization of case management services is required. The supervisor shall attest to the accuracy of the documentation by a personal signature to include credentials and title. Each beneficiary record must reflect supervisory review every 4 weeks at a minimum. The frequency of the reviews must be increased if the findings warrant such action. The review must include the following: the beneficiary record to assure that all required paperwork as defined by this policy is in the record and progress notes must be reviewed for compliance with the requirements in Subsections 7.5 and 7.6. The billing must be checked for accuracy to assure it corresponds to the progress notes. This is not billable case management time.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.2.5
Title: 6.2.5 Decertification
Section: 6.2.5
Policy: 12B
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Case Management](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched documentation.
Content:
If any one of the following conditions is substantiated, the provider may be decertified by NC Medicaid, or DHHS designated contractor, and dis-enrolled by NC Medicaid. This list is not all inclusive.
Failure to provide core service components.
Fraudulent billing practices.
Owner(s) being convicted of a felony charge.
Failure to develop, submit, and implement a written plan of correction to resolve unmet program requirements cited by NC Medicaid, or DHHS designated contractor; to make recommended corrections; or both within 30 calendar days.
Falsification of records.
Violation of a beneficiary's confidentiality.
Employment of staff who do not meet the criteria stated in Subsection 6.1.
Failure of staff to complete NC Medicaid, or DHHS designated contractor, mandatory basic training within 90 days of their employment date.
Failure of staff to obtain required continuing educational units (CEU), as specified in Subsection 6.1.
Failure to provide case management staff with supervision to meet the beneficiaries' needs.
Failure to submit any required documentation within the time frame designated by this policy, NC Medicaid or DHHS designated contractor, or both.
Failure to provide documentation as specified in Subsection 7.5 that is sufficient to support the provider's billing.
Failure to implement and enforce a quality improvement program.
Failure to notify NC Medicaid, or DHHS designated contractor, within 30 calendar days of proposed changes, or five business days of actual changes, of any changes in agency name, director or ownership, mailing address, and telephone number(s), resulting in NC Medicaid or DHHS designated contractors, inability to contact the provider.
Failure to comply with all applicable federal and state laws, regulations, state reimbursement plan, and policies governing the services authorized under the Medicaid program.
Failure of a provider to enroll any beneficiaries within four months of certification.
Failure of a provider to achieve or maintain the requirements for certification as defined in Subsection 6.2 of this policy.
When NC Medicaid, or NC Medicaid's designated agent, notifies a Medicaidenrolled provider that he is no longer certified to provide HIV Case Management services, the provider may request a reconsideration review in accordance with 10A NCAC 22F.0402.

ID: sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.1.7.1
Title: 6.1.7.1 Training for Case Managers and Supervisors
Section: 6.1.7.1
Policy: 12B
Type: clinical_policy
Citation link: [Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Case Management](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/12b-human-immunodeficiency-virus-hiv-case-management/download?attachment)
Reason: Matched documentation.
Content:
All HIV case managers and case management supervisors shall complete North Carolina state-sponsored, basic training within 90 days of their employment date, and must be completed prior to any billed case management units. It is the responsibility of providers to retain copies of certificates of completion issued by NC Medicaid or DHHS designated contractor.
Upon successful completion of basic training, the CM or supervisor will be able to perform all the following:
describe basic HIV information and prevention techniques;
describe the scope of work for CMs;
identify and explain the core components of HIV Case Management;
demonstrate an understanding of basic ethical issues relating to case management;
demonstrate an understanding of the responsibilities and functions of the HIV CM system of care; and
demonstrate an understanding of the documentation requirements of this program as defined in Subsections 7.5 and 7.6 .
